name: False sharing fix: alignas(64) per-thread result slots
listed_description: Padding each thread's private accumulator to its own 64-byte cache line so eight threads summing random numbers stop invalidating each other's cache lines.
claim_text: Unaligned eight-thread sum took 4403 milliseconds; aligned to 64 bytes took 160 milliseconds (about 27x faster).
book_benchmark: Eight pinned std::thread workers each do 100 million mt19937 draws and add to a per-thread unsigned long; adjacent 8-byte slots versus alignas(64) slots; wall clock via std::chrono; GCC 13 and Clang 18 available, GCC with libstdc++ used; AMD Ryzen Threadripper Pro 5975WX, Ubuntu 24.04. Book also shows perf stat: 96.63% cache misses unaligned versus 27.21% aligned. Code in the book's companion repository (13x07-false_sharing).
found_in: book: Asynchronous Programming with C++ (2024), ch. 13, section False sharing

name: SPSC lock-free ring buffer with cached head and tail indices
listed_description: Single-producer single-consumer lock-free queue where each side keeps a private copy of the other side's index and re-reads the shared atomic only when the queue looks full or empty, cutting cache coherency traffic; head and tail also separated by alignas(64).
claim_text: Throughput rose from about 101.6 million to about 162.5 million ops/sec, roughly 60% faster; cache misses fell from 41.30% to 31.39%.
book_benchmark: Producer and consumer threads push/pop ring buffer (power-of-two capacity), ops/sec counted by the book's harness, perf stat cache-references and cache-misses; baseline is the book's own queue before adding cached indices (head_ and tail_ already aligned to 64 bytes); AMD Ryzen Threadripper Pro 5975WX, Ubuntu 24.04, GCC 13. Code in the companion repository (13x09-spsc_lock_free_queue). Not compared against Boost.Lockfree, rigtorp SPSCQueue or a mutex queue in this chunk.
found_in: book: Asynchronous Programming with C++ (2024), ch. 13, section SPSC lock-free queue

name: uberlog
